screening_results.reason: This is an empirical human structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) that reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray matter density changes between smokers and never-smoker controls. Methods include acquisition of T1-weighted images (1.5T), preprocessing and tensor-based morphometry with SPM5, and between-group contrasts (UQ vs NS, SQ vs NS) reported in text and Supplementary Table S2. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength, and analysis software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and contains original voxelwise whole-brain results suitable for coordinate extraction. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations.
